SPECIFICATION FOR 




IRON-NICKEL ALLOY 36 FOR CERAMIC SEALING 




1. Scope — Covers the requirements of wrought Iron-nickel alloy 36 in the form of wires, rounds 




and strips intended primarily for sealing ceramics and for other applications like electronic compo- 




nents, relays, aircraft controls, optical instruments, metrology instruments, etc. Tubings are not 




included under this specification. 




2. Supply of Material — The general requirements relating to supply of the material shall con- 




form to IS : 1387-1967 'General requirements for the supply of metallurgical materials ( //>5f 




revision )'. 




3. Chemical Composition — The chemical composition of the material, when determined by 




gravimetric or spectrochemical analysis, shall be as follows:

4.2 Lengths of Supply for Wires and Rounds — For thinner gauge wires ( 005 to O'B mm 
diameter ), small spools are normally used where total mass of wire not exceeding 1 5 kg of 
continuous length will be wound.

4.3 Straightness — Wires and rounds supplied in cut lengths shall be straight and free from bends 
and twists. The deviation in straightness shall not be more than 3 mm for a length of one metre. 

5. Freedom from Defects 

5.1 Iron-nickel alloy 36 supplied in various forms shall be free from scale, corrosion, cracks, seams 
scratches, slivers and other surface defects. The materials shall be uniform In cross- section, 
chemical composition, finish and temper. 

5.2 All lubricants used in processing shall be thoroughly removed by the manufacturer. Protec- 
tive coatings present on the material, as shipped, shall be readily removable by any of the common 
organic solvents such as trichloroethylene. 

6. Grain Size — Iron-nickel alloy 36 strip and sheet for deep drawing applications shall have an 
average grain size of less than 0065 mm or 16 grains/254 mm^ of image at a magnification of 
100. For material less than 0*13 mm in thickness, the grain size shall be such that there are no 
less than 4 grains across the thickness. 

7. Thermal Expansion — The average linear coefficient of thermal expansion for iron-nickel 
alloy 36 shall be as indicated in Table 2, when tested with a precision diiatometer in accordance 
with 15:3410-1965 ^Method of test for determining coefficient of linear expansion of metals 
at different temperature ranges'. 

TABLE 2 THERMAL EXPANSION REQUIREMENTS 
Temperature Range, Linear Coefficient of Thermal Expansion, 

Oto 50 < 1*2 

20to100 1*2 

20 to 150 1-6 

20 to 200 2*2 

20 to 300 46 

20 to 400 7*5 



8. Porosity — Iron-nickel alloy 36 rounds of diameters higher than 12 mm shall be normally free 
from porosity when tested in a helium leak detector. Porosity requirements shall be specified by 
the purchasers only for critical end use applications and this shall be subject to mutual agreement 
between the manufacturer and the purchaser.

10. Hardness — iron-nickel alloy 36 strips and sheets intended for deep drawing applications 
shall be supplied in cold roiled and annealed condition. The hardness shall not exceed Rockwell 
B 82 ( HV 149 ) when deternnined in accordance with 13:1586-1968 'Methods for Rockwell 
hardness test ( B and C scales ) for steels ( first rev/s/on )'. 

10.1 Physical and mechanical properties have also been given in Appendix A for information 
only. 

11. Packing and Marking 

11.1 Wires and strips supplied in coils shall be wrapped all around with a polyethylene lined 
hessian cloth. The coils up to 1*5 mm wire diameter shall be packed in wooden cases to avoid 
damage during transit. Wires of smaller diameter supplied in spools shall be packed in polyethy- 
lene bags with small quantity of silica-gel for moisture absorption. 

1 1.2 Rods and sheets supplied in cut lengths shall be covered in hessian and subsequently packed 
in wooden cases. 

11.3 The wooden cases shall be indelibly marked with the manufacturer's name, mass, dimen- 
sions, batch number and description of the items. 

11.4 The material may also be marked with the Standard Mark. Details are available with the 
Bureau of Indian Standards. 

12. Basis of Purchase — Orders for materials under the specification shall include the following 
informations: 

a) Description and size, 

b) Surface finish, 

c) Packing and marking, and 

d) Specification number.

This alloy can be welded by MIG, TIG, plasma and resistance welding. The filter rod should 
be preferably of the same composition for obtaining optimum joint characteristics. Heavily coated 
18-8 stainless steel or mild steel filler rods can also be used. The welded parts shall be stress 
relieved by annealing them at 350''C for 2 hours.

WELDABILITY 





EXPLANATORY NOTE 

Iron-nickel alloy 36 is a controlled expansion alloy for ceramic sealing having a lowest 
thermal expansion of approximately one tenth that of carbon steel up to 200''C. The important 
characteristics of this alloy are uniform magnetic and mechanical properties, low coercive field 
strength, controlled thermal expansion and low contents of non-metallic inclusions. This alloy 
finds applications in electronic components, relays, aircraft controls, optical instruments, cryogenic 
parts, metrology instruments, precision pendulums, temperature regulators and thermostatic 
bimetal strips. This alloy is recommended for use where the continuous operating temperature 
does not exceed 200°C. 

This standard has been prepared as a guide to the manufacturers and users of iron- 
nickel alloy 36 which is familiarly known as INVAR. In the preparation of this standard, 
necessary assistance has been derived from TGL 24329-1984 Controlled Expansion Alloys 
Semiconductors.
